fullPassage: Most of the bacteria in our guts are absolutely essential for us. Without them, we would be unable to acquire the nutrients we need to maintain life. Like the gut microbes that allow ruminants to digest leaves, they help process nutrients into a form that we can absorb through the gut wall. For a species like humans that has an energetically very expensive super-large brain, this is crucial. They also help train the immune system to distinguish between friendly bacteria and viruses and the pathogenic ones that daily invade our bodies. Without them we would be cognitively deficient, emotionally unstable, and at the mercy of the many diseases that constantly attack us.

questions.passage: Most of the bacteria in our guts are absolutely (A)[essential / harmful] for us. Without them, we would be unable to (B)[acquire / reject] the nutrients we need to maintain life. Like the gut microbes that allow ruminants to digest leaves, they help process nutrients into a form that we can (C)[absorb / block] through the gut wall. For a species like humans that has an energetically very expensive super-large brain, this is crucial. They also help train the immune system to distinguish between friendly bacteria and viruses and the pathogenic ones that daily invade our bodies. Without them we would be cognitively deficient, emotionally unstable, and at the mercy of the many diseases that constantly attack us.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① essential - acquire - absorb: 장내 박테리아가 우리에게 '필수적이고', 영양분을 '얻게' 해주며, 장벽을 통해 '흡수할' 수 있게 해준다는 원문 내용.
❌ ② harmful - acquire - absorb: '해로운'은 essential(필수적)의 반의어로 원문 맥락과 모순.
❌ ③ essential - reject - absorb: '거부하다'는 영양분을 '얻는' 기능과 반대.
❌ ④ essential - acquire - block: '차단하다'는 '흡수하다'의 반대로 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: essential(필수적인) ↔ harmful(해로운). acquire(얻다) ↔ reject(거부하다). absorb(흡수하다) ↔ block(차단하다)

Like the gut microbes that allow ruminants to (A)[digest / reject] leaves, they help (B)[process / waste] nutrients into a form that we can absorb through the gut wall. For a species like humans that has an energetically very (C)[expensive / cheap] super-large brain, this is crucial. They also help train the immune system to distinguish between friendly bacteria and viruses and the pathogenic ones that daily invade our bodies. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ digest - process - expensive: 반추동물이 잎을 '소화하고', 영양분을 '처리하며', 인간의 대뇌는 에너지적으로 '비용이 많이 드는' 기관이라는 원문 내용.
❌ ① reject - process - expensive: '거부하다'는 '소화'의 반대 개념.
❌ ② digest - waste - expensive: '낭비하다'는 영양분을 유용한 형태로 '처리'한다는 내용과 모순.
❌ ④ digest - process - cheap: '저렴한'은 super-large brain을 'very expensive'로 묘사한 원문과 반대.
det.tip: digest(소화하다) ↔ reject(거부하다). process(처리하다) ↔ waste(낭비하다). energetically expensive = 에너지를 많이 소비하는

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② distinguish - pathogenic - attack: 면역체계가 유익균과 병원균을 '구별하고', '병원성의' 것들이 몸을 침입하며, 질병이 우리를 '공격한다'는 원문 내용.
❌ ① confuse - pathogenic - attack: '혼동하다'는 면역체계가 구별하도록 돕는다는 내용과 모순.
❌ ③ distinguish - harmless - attack: '무해한'은 pathogenic(병원성의)의 반의어로 원문과 반대.
❌ ④ distinguish - pathogenic - protect: '보호하다'는 질병이 우리를 공격한다는 부정적 맥락과 모순.
det.tip: distinguish(구별하다) ↔ confuse(혼동하다). pathogenic(병원성의) ↔ harmless(무해한). attack(공격하다) ↔ protect(보호하다)

det.tip: distinguish between A and B = A와 B를 구별하다. 면역체계의 핵심 기능은 아군과 적군 구별.

questions.passage: Most of the bacteria in our guts are absolutely essential for us. Without them, we would be unable to acquire the nutrients we need to maintain life. Like the gut microbes that allow ruminants to digest leaves, they help process nutrients into a form that we can absorb through the gut wall. For a species like humans that has an energetically very expensive super-large brain, __________. They also help train the immune system to distinguish between friendly bacteria and viruses and the pathogenic ones that daily invade our bodies. Without them we would be cognitively deficient, emotionally unstable, and at the mercy of the many diseases that constantly attack us.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ efficient nutrient absorption is extremely important: 에너지 소모가 큰 대뇌를 유지하려면 효율적 영양 흡수가 필수라는 맥락.
❌ ① larger brains are always unnecessary: 본문은 큰 뇌를 긍정적으로 다룸. 모순.
❌ ② gut bacteria are dangerous to health: 본문 전체 메시지와 정반대.
❌ ④ ruminants have smaller brains than humans: 반추동물은 비교 대상일 뿐 본문 주제가 아님.
det.tip: energetically expensive super-large brain = 에너지가 많이 드는 초대형 뇌 → 효율적 영양 공급 필요

questions.passage: Most of the bacteria in our guts are absolutely essential for us. Without them, we would be unable to acquire the nutrients we need to maintain life. Like the gut microbes that allow ruminants to digest leaves, they help process nutrients into a form that we can absorb through the gut wall. For a species like humans that has an energetically very expensive super-large brain, this is crucial. They also help train the immune system to distinguish between friendly bacteria and viruses and the pathogenic ones that daily invade our bodies. Without gut bacteria, humans would __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ suffer cognitively and emotionally while being vulnerable to diseases: 본문 마지막 'cognitively deficient, emotionally unstable, at the mercy of diseases'와 일치.
❌ ① develop larger brains: 본문은 영양 부족으로 뇌 기능 저하를 시사.
❌ ② become more resistant to infection: 면역 훈련 기능 상실로 오히려 취약해짐.
❌ ③ digest leaves like ruminants: 반추동물과의 유사성은 비교일 뿐 인간의 결과가 아님.
det.tip: Without them = gut bacteria 없이. 결과: cognitive deficiency, emotional instability, disease vulnerability

ch: suffer cognitively and emotionally while being vulnerable to diseases
